title: Board-pattern readiness test — most-repeated question types
chapter: CBSE Class 12 Economics (030) · all eight units, weighted by the 2026-27 theory marks
tagline: Practice questions modelled on past CBSE papers; not predictions of this year's paper.
disclaimer: Original questions written for Teraminds Academy from the NCERT textbooks prescribed for 2026-27, modelled on the most-repeated question types in CBSE board papers 2023–26 and the Sample Question Paper 2026-27 (see our Board Blueprint). A board-pattern readiness test for practice only: not a prediction of any exam and no promise of marks.
instructions: 37 questions. MCQ and assertion-reason: choose one option. Numeric: type a whole number (no commas or ₹ needed).

U1.name: A1 · National Income and Related Aggregates (10 marks)
U1.tip: NNP_FC = GDP_MP − depreciation + NFIA − net indirect taxes. Value added = value of output (sales + change in stock) − intermediate consumption. Real GDP = nominal GDP ÷ price index × 100. Count final goods only. GDP is not a full welfare index: distribution, non-monetary exchanges and externalities.
U1.ncert: NCERT Introductory Macroeconomics (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 2 National Income Accounting

U2.name: A2 · Money and Banking (6 marks)
U2.tip: Money multiplier = 1/LRR; total deposits = initial deposit × 1/LRR. Repo rate = rate at which RBI lends to commercial banks. To curb inflation: raise CRR/repo, sell securities (OMO).
U2.ncert: NCERT Introductory Macroeconomics (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 3 Money and Banking

U3.name: A3 · Determination of Income and Employment (12 marks)
U3.tip: MPC + MPS = 1; k = 1/(1 − MPC) = 1/MPS; ΔY = k × ΔI. Equilibrium: Y = C + I, so with C = c̄ + bY, Y = (c̄ + I)/(1 − b). Deficient demand: raise spending, cut repo/bank rate.
U3.ncert: NCERT Introductory Macroeconomics (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 4 Determination of Income and Employment

U4.name: A4 · Government Budget and the Economy (6 marks)
U4.tip: Capital receipts create a liability or reduce assets (borrowing, disinvestment). Fiscal deficit = total expenditure − (revenue receipts + non-debt capital receipts); primary deficit = fiscal deficit − interest payments; revenue deficit = revenue expenditure − revenue receipts.
U4.ncert: NCERT Introductory Macroeconomics (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 5 Government Budget and the Economy

U5.name: A5 · Balance of Payments (6 marks)
U5.tip: Current account: goods, services, transfers, income. Capital account: FDI, portfolio investment, loans. Accommodating items (reserve changes) cover a BoP gap. Depreciation of the rupee makes Indian exports cheaper abroad.
U5.ncert: NCERT Introductory Macroeconomics (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 6 Open Economy Macroeconomics

U6.name: B6 · Development Experience (1947-90) and Reforms since 1991 (12 marks)
U6.tip: On the eve of independence India exported raw materials and imported finished goods; Britain controlled over half its trade. Plan goals: growth, modernisation, self-reliance, equity. IPR 1956: three categories of industries. Green Revolution: HYV seeds + fertilisers + irrigation. 1991 reforms followed a foreign-exchange (BoP) crisis.
U6.ncert: NCERT Indian Economic Development (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 1 Indian Economy on the Eve of Independence, Ch 2 Indian Economy 1950-1990, Ch 3 Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation

U7.name: B7 · Current Challenges facing the Indian Economy (20 marks)
U7.tip: Human capital: education, health, on-the-job training, migration, information. Rural credit: NABARD (1982), SHGs/micro-credit; Amul = cooperative success. Worker-population ratio = workers ÷ population × 100. Casualisation and jobless growth. Sustainable development: don't exceed the environment's absorptive or carrying capacity.
U7.ncert: NCERT Indian Economic Development (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 4 Human Capital Formation, Ch 5 Rural Development, Ch 6 Employment, Ch 7 Environment and Sustainable Development

U8.name: B8 · India and its Neighbours (8 marks)
U8.tip: China: Great Leap Forward 1958, reforms 1978, one-child policy; growth led by manufacturing. Pakistan: reforms 1988. India: growth led by services.
U8.ncert: NCERT Indian Economic Development (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 8 Comparative Development Experiences of India and its Neighbours

questions.question: GDP at market price = ₹1,000 crore, depreciation = ₹100 crore, net factor income from abroad = −₹20 crore and net indirect taxes = ₹80 crore. Find NNP at factor cost, in ₹ crore.

questions.question: Which of these is a STOCK concept?
questions.explanation: A stock is measured at a point of time (wealth, capital); a flow over a period (income, investment, depreciation).
questions.remediation: A1 · National Income and Related Aggregates (10 marks): NCERT Introductory Macroeconomics (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 2 National Income Accounting; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: Smoke from a factory harms nearby residents, but they are not compensated. In national income terms this is:
questions.explanation: Externalities are not paid for, so they are not in GDP: one reason GDP is not a perfect index of welfare.
questions.remediation: A1 · National Income and Related Aggregates (10 marks): NCERT Introductory Macroeconomics (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 2 National Income Accounting; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
options: Counted as a deduction from GDP
A factor payment included in NFIA
A negative externality that GDP does not account for, so GDP overstates welfare

questions.question: Banks keep 20% of deposits as reserves (LRR = 0.2). If an initial deposit of ₹1,000 is made, what are the total deposits created, in ₹?
questions.explanation: Money multiplier = 1/0.2 = 5; total deposits = 1000 × 5 = 5000.
questions.remediation: A2 · Money and Banking (6 marks): NCERT Introductory Macroeconomics (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 3 Money and Banking; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: The repo rate is the rate at which:
questions.explanation: Repo = RBI lends to banks (against securities); parking funds with the RBI earns the reverse repo rate.
questions.remediation: A2 · Money and Banking (6 marks): NCERT Introductory Macroeconomics (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 3 Money and Banking; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
options: The government borrows from the public
The RBI lends to commercial banks for short periods
Commercial banks lend to the public
Commercial banks park surplus funds with the RBI

questions.question: To reduce inflation, the RBI is most likely to:
questions.explanation: Selling securities absorbs reserves from banks and reduces money supply; the others expand money supply.
questions.remediation: A2 · Money and Banking (6 marks): NCERT Introductory Macroeconomics (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 3 Money and Banking; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.
options: Sell government securities in the open market

questions.question: Which measure would help correct a situation of deficient demand?
questions.explanation: Deficient demand needs more spending: cheaper credit (lower repo/bank rate), buying securities, more government expenditure or lower taxes.
questions.remediation: A3 · Determination of Income and Employment (12 marks): NCERT Introductory Macroeconomics (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 4 Determination of Income and Employment; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: Which of these is a capital receipt of the government?
questions.explanation: Disinvestment reduces government assets, so it is a capital receipt; the others are revenue receipts.

questions.question: Total government expenditure = ₹1,000 crore, revenue receipts = ₹600 crore, non-debt capital receipts = ₹100 crore and interest payments = ₹120 crore. Find the primary deficit, in ₹ crore.
questions.explanation: Fiscal deficit = 1000 − (600 + 100) = 300; primary deficit = 300 − 120 = 180.
questions.remediation: A4 · Government Budget and the Economy (6 marks): NCERT Introductory Macroeconomics (Class 12, 2026-27): Ch 5 Government Budget and the Economy; then the question types listed for this unit in the Blueprint PDF.

questions.question: Choose the correct option.

questions.assertion: A high revenue deficit is a warning sign for the government.
questions.reason: It means the government is borrowing to finance consumption expenditure, which creates no assets to repay the debt.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false

questions.question: Which transaction is recorded in the capital account of India's balance of payments?

questions.question: Accommodating transactions in the balance of payments are those that:
